title: Water in a plastic bag over an open flame

lines: This bag is full of water. I'm about to hold it over an open flame.
Empty bag first. One second... gone.
Now the one with water. Same flame. Nothing. It just starts to boil.
That flame is over a thousand degrees. The plastic melts at one twenty. So why is it fine?
Water is a heat sponge. Heat hitting the plastic gets pulled into the water faster than the plastic can heat up.
And water has a hard ceiling. At a hundred degrees it boils, and refuses to get hotter. The extra energy just makes steam.
So the plastic never gets hotter than the water touching it. A hundred degrees. Twenty short of melting.
Same reason you can boil water in a paper cup. Follow for more physics that looks fake.
